recognize_zh: S100 免疫染色中大型組織球的細胞核與細胞質呈強棕色陽性，中央一顆 S100 陽性組織球內包著數個未染色的藍色淋巴球核，突顯 emperipolesis；周圍小淋巴球為陰性，符合 Rosai-Dorfman disease。
features: Strong nuclear and cytoplasmic brown S100 staining in large histiocytes with abundant cytoplasm
Central S100-positive histiocyte outlines several engulfed, S100-negative lymphocytes, highlighting emperipolesis
Background small lymphocytes are negative with blue hematoxylin counterstain
Diffuse granular brown staining in interstitial histiocytic cytoplasm between lymphocytes
Engulfed cells have intact round nuclei within the stained cytoplasm
describe_en: S100 immunohistochemistry shows strong nuclear and cytoplasmic positivity in large histiocytes. The stain outlines histiocytes containing multiple intact, S100-negative lymphocytes within their cytoplasm, accentuating emperipolesis, while the background small lymphocytes are negative. Findings are consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease, which is further characterized by OCT2 and cyclin D1 positivity with CD1a and langerin negativity in the lesional histiocytes.

ddx.vs: Also S100 positive, but lesional cells are CD1a and langerin positive with grooved nuclei and no emperipolesis.
S100-positive spindle to ovoid cells form fascicles or whorls with atypia and lack the engulfed lymphocytes seen here.
Shows S100 positivity in cohesive atypical cells with macronucleoli that also express SOX10, HMB45 or Melan-A.
Sinus histiocytes are S100 negative (CD68/CD163 positive) and lack emperipolesis.
